paper.title: T-InvBlocks: what invertibility can and cannot preserve

claims.claim: Each later branch reads already updated earlier branches. This triangular dependence makes inversion possible without inverting the convolutional subnetworks themselves. The diagram does not imply the three streams are independent: deliberate cross-stream interaction is the whole point.

T-SAIN replaces blocks in both f and g while retaining the asymmetric compression-aware framework. The actual JPEG codec is not rendered invertible by the surrounding network. Its inverse simulator is a learned correction for expected corruption. The zero-latent strategy removes sampling, but deterministic output is not equivalent to authentic detail recovery.

At ×2, DIV2K improves 44.32→45.46 dB while parameters decrease 1.67→1.57M. At ×4, Urban100 declines 31.41→31.19 dB and parameters increase 4.35→4.67M; DIV2K improves only 35.07→35.10. Thus the evidence supports substantial ×2 gains, not uniform superiority or uniformly smaller models. These are means without seed-level uncertainty intervals.

At ×4 and QF70, the score rises 29.83→30.34 dB; at QF90 it rises 30.31→30.92 dB, with 5.45M versus 6.49M parameters. This supports compression-aware transfer beyond the QF75 training setting. The +0.61 dB endpoint also shows why the prose’s approximate “0.2–0.5 dB” should not replace exact table values. Only the tested JPEG pipeline is covered, not arbitrary bitrates, codecs or chroma subsampling choices.

On DIV2K, baseline IRN scores 44.32; color conversion alone falls to 44.02, zero-only rises to 45.18, and full T-IRN reaches 45.46. Most of this particular gain already appears with zero-latent training; the remaining +0.28 dB accompanies the block redesign. Because there is no complete factorial comparison of every component combination at identical parameterization, this cannot assign an independent causal contribution to every coupling function.

At QF80, SAIN gives 30.13, color conversion 30.47, zero-only 30.12, and T-SAIN 30.69 dB. Unlike the uncompressed experiment, zero alone does not help here. The evidence supports a context-dependent interaction between color handling, compression and coupling, rather than a universal claim that sampling always harms reconstruction.

The feather and building-grid crops illustrate sharper recovered structure under compression. They help interpret the numerical gains but remain selected examples, not a rate of artifact-free restoration. Their two quality settings also cannot isolate the effect of each individual block.
